bridges.description: Support God's existence through the cumulative force of the selected arguments.
Connect cosmic origin, fine-tuning and morality to a personal good creator.
Use resurrection and defeater-sensitive experience to support Christian theism.
Support fallible disbelief by arguing that the evidence fits better without God.
Challenge divine explanation through natural reality, moral realism and suffering.
Challenge sectarian experience and historical inference as reliable routes to truth.

sections.title: Cosmic origin and causation
sections.rationale: Whether all physical reality began, whether beginning requires a cause, and whether that cause is personal form Craig's primary cosmological route and Nugent's most sustained reply.

sections.title: Fine-tuning and design
sections.rationale: The life-permitting range, the proposed necessity/chance/design alternatives, and the random-observer objection form a distinct probabilistic design exchange.

sections.title: Divine mind, change and freedom
sections.rationale: The coherence of an unembodied creator, creation by a reportedly changeless being, emergence of consciousness, and foreknowledge versus freedom are distinct attribute questions.

sections.title: Evil and comparative probability
sections.rationale: The speakers separately dispute logical compatibility of God with evil and whether suffering, cosmic scale, and other facts are probabilistically more expected without God.

sections.title: Objective moral grounding
sections.rationale: The existence, genealogy, knowledge, and normative grounding of objective duties are disputed through divine nature, evolution, and impartial rational choice.

sections.title: Divine commands and moral application
sections.rationale: The Euthyphro extension, evil-God reversal, commanded killing, and deathbed repentance test whether the proposed divine moral order is nonarbitrary and just.

sections.title: Resurrection, experience and method
sections.rationale: The resurrection case, personal religious experience, comparative defeaters, and evidential method distinguish Christian theism and test its warrant.

moves.warrant: Craig cites philosophical and scientific considerations for a finite past and says something cannot arise from nothing.

retainedSpeechCoverage.omissions: Craig's detailed finite-past illustrations, numerical fine-tuning comparisons, historical names, devotional elaboration, and closing burden recap are omitted as subordinate support. selectionBalanceAudit.rationale: The evil-probability section has four con contributions because Nugent separately argues from a perfect creator, purposive physical tuning, cosmic scale and human marginality, and then renews the suffering-free-world challenge after Craig's logical reply; Craig supplies distinct logical and overall-probability responses. The command section contains four con developments—opening Euthyphro/evil-God symmetry, scriptural-corruption examples, renewed nature/privation reversal, and killing-plus-repentance consistency—against two Craig replies. Fine-tuning is pro-heavier because Craig separates parameter improbability from the random-observer multiverse objection. The overall difference follows these nonmergeable source stages rather than forced symmetry.

The con fourth row is authorized because evil-world—Suffering is offered as evidence against the proposed creator; natural-reality-fit—The physical fine-tuning data do not uniquely fit a divine purpose; cosmic-scale-and-human-marginality—Those observations are offered as comparative evidence against a special human-centered divine plan; renewed-suffering-free-world-reply—If a perfect God could create a suffering-free world, the evidential challenge remains; each is a distinct independently assessable inference.

The pro fourth row is authorized because morality-god—Atheistic moral genealogy is said not to supply normative authority; moral-experience-objectivity—Together with his grounding premise, objective moral experience is said to entail God; rational-committee-normativity-critique—Craig presents the committee model as presupposing the normativity it must explain, while the inventory records that his characterization conflicts with Nugent's stated moral realism; normative-grounding-reply—Objective duties require a transcendent ground; each is a distinct independently assessable inference. The con fourth row is authorized because natural-objective-morality—Evolution can explain moral cognition without committing Nugent to moral nihilism; species-inclusive-impartial-contract—Independence from each chooser's personal position is offered as a non-theistic route to objective justice; moral-premise-challenge—A coherent non-theistic model blocks the inference to God; pure-reason-impartiality-response—This supplies a non-theistic proposal for objective right and wrong; each is a distinct independently assessable inference.

The con fourth row is authorized because euthyphro-evil-god—Theism needs a reason to privilege ultimate goodness; religion-corrupts-morality—God-belief is not necessary for morality and can impede it; renewed-evil-god-and-nature-reply—Craig's nature and privation answers are said not to break the symmetry; command-killing-and-repentance-challenge—Unanswered internal consistency challenges count against the claimed perfectly good moral source without presupposing Nugent's own ontology; each is a distinct independently assessable inference.

The con fourth row is authorized because fallible-atheism-method—The supernatural authority claim, rather than deductive atheism, bears the principal justificatory burden; reason-over-conflicting-faith—Divergence under faith and potential convergence under evidence count against Craig's experiential route; experience-comparative-caution—The cumulative case warrants caution rather than automatic rejection; resurrection-development—That development supplies a nonmiraculous reason to resist Craig's inference; each is a distinct independently assessable inference.
